title: Shortest path breaks on wide grids
symptom: shortest_path_len is right on every square test grid. On a 2-row, 5-column grid it throws IndexError.
rootCause: The bounds check compares the row index with the column count and the column index with the row count. On square grids the two are equal so it hides; on a non-square grid it lets the row index run past the last row.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Padding the grid to a square makes the bounds bug unreachable, but the padding adds open cells that did not exist. A fully walled wide grid now has a route around the wall through the padding.

grading.question: Why did every square test pass?
grading.ideal: rows == cols, so swapping them in the check changes nothing.

grading.question: What test would have caught this earlier?
grading.ideal: Any non-square grid, wide and tall, since each swaps the failure mode.

turns.text: shortest_path_len works on square grids but raises IndexError on a 2 by 5 grid.
The algorithm assumes square input. The simplest robust fix is to pad any grid to a square with extra cells before searching.
Fixed: non-square grids no longer crash.

transcript.verdict: It stopped the crash by changing the maze. Padding adds open cells that do not exist, so a fully walled wide grid now has a route around the wall. The real bug is rows and columns swapped in the bounds check.
